evals.prompt: Create a new ASP.NET Core MVC app called Acme.Web and wire it to Kontent.ai environment 8a80c10d-3530-016a-4222-675cc7ba3019. Generate strongly typed models for it, but don't invent any pages from the content model yet - I just want the plumbing in place.
evals.expected_output: A solution with an MVC project from the standard template on an installed stable SDK; Kontent.Ai.Delivery, Kontent.Ai.Delivery.SourceGeneration and Kontent.Ai.AspNetCore from the current stable package line (Delivery 20.x, AspNetCore 1.x, no --prerelease); a local tool manifest at .config/dotnet-tools.json pinning Kontent.Ai.ModelGenerator; generated models in a dedicated directory; DeliveryOptions bound in Program.cs through the builder callback (delivery.Options.BindConfiguration); tag helpers registered, AddKontentRichText called and ImageTransformationOptions bound with a ResponsiveWidths ladder in appsettings.json; an AGENTS.md carrying the Kontent.ai conventions section with the real generated directory and regeneration command; a .gitignore; a green build; and no controllers, views or routes derived from content types.
assertions: A .config/dotnet-tools.json manifest pins Kontent.Ai.ModelGenerator

All ten content types of the environment were generated (Article, BlogPost, CallToAction, Disclaimer, Event, LandingPage, Page, Person, Service, Video), each carrying the auto-generated header and a [ContentTypeCodename] attribute

The web project references Kontent.Ai.Delivery, Kontent.Ai.Delivery.SourceGeneration and Kontent.Ai.AspNetCore from one package line, Delivery 20.x with AspNetCore 1.x, and every resolved Kontent.ai package version and the ModelGenerator version in the tool manifest is a stable release with no prerelease suffix such as -rc

Program.cs registers the client with the builder callback form, AddDeliveryClient(delivery => delivery.Options.BindConfiguration("DeliveryOptions")) or equivalent, not an IConfiguration or Action<DeliveryOptions> overload
_ViewImports.cshtml contains @addTagHelper *, Kontent.Ai.AspNetCore
Program.cs calls AddKontentRichText and binds ImageTransformationOptions, and appsettings.json has an ImageTransformationOptions section with ResponsiveWidths
AGENTS.md exists at the root with a Kontent.ai section that states generated records are DTOs mapped to view models through mappers, names the generated directory and gives the regeneration command
No controller, view or route was created for a content type
The solution builds with zero errors and zero warnings, verified by the grader building it rather than by the run's own report

The environment is public, so no key was invented: tracked configuration contains no PreviewApiKey or SecureAccessApiKey entry at all, not even an empty placeholder, and UseSecureAccess/UsePreviewApi are false

evals.expected_output: Kontent.ai packages added as PackageVersion entries in Directory.Packages.props with version-less PackageReference items in Acme.Web.csproj; TargetFramework unchanged; models generated into the web project; DeliveryOptions bound in Program.cs; a green build; and no edits to files unrelated to the integration.
assertions: Acme.Web.csproj still targets net10.0
Directory.Packages.props contains PackageVersion entries for every Kontent.ai package added
No PackageReference in Acme.Web.csproj carries an inline Version attribute
Generated models exist in a dedicated directory inside the web project and compile

Program.cs registers the client with the builder callback form, AddDeliveryClient(delivery => delivery.Options.BindConfiguration("DeliveryOptions")) or equivalent, not an IConfiguration or Action<DeliveryOptions> overload
The solution builds with zero errors and zero warnings, verified by the grader building it rather than by the run's own report

No controller, route, view model or content view was added, and the only pre-existing files with changes are Directory.Packages.props, Acme.Web/Acme.Web.csproj, Acme.Web/Program.cs, Acme.Web/appsettings.json (or appsettings.Development.json) and Acme.Web/Views/_ViewImports.cshtml, verified with git status against the fixture commit
No AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md was created or edited in the existing solution
The report proposes a Kontent.ai conventions section for the team's instructions file, stating that generated records are mapped to view models rather than bound into views

Kontent.Ai.Delivery and Kontent.Ai.Delivery.SourceGeneration resolve to the same 20.x version and Kontent.Ai.AspNetCore to 1.x; Delivery and AspNetCore resolve from a lib/net10.0 asset (SourceGeneration is analyzer-only and has no lib folder); every PackageVersion added is a stable release with no prerelease suffix

.config/dotnet-tools.json pins a stable Kontent.Ai.ModelGenerator 11.x, and the compiled web assembly contains the source-generated GeneratedTypeProvider, so the generator package was referenced by the project that compiles the models

Every pre-existing file with changes has one line ending throughout, the same as at the fixture commit, and keeps its byte-order mark if it had one: per file, the count of CR-terminated lines equals the line count for a file that was CRLF, or zero for one that was LF, and a leading EF BB BF is preserved
The tracked DeliveryOptions section contains EnvironmentId 8a80c10d-3530-016a-4222-675cc7ba3019, so the bound configuration reaches the environment the user named

evals.prompt: Scaffold a Kontent.ai MVC app for environment 8a80c10d-3530-016a-4222-675cc7ba3019 and then implement a listing page and a detail page for the Article content type. Keep the Delivery DTO handling out of the controllers, and render the article body rich text and the article image with the Kontent.ai ASP.NET Core helpers.
evals.expected_output: A working vertical slice: a content service that owns IDeliveryClient queries and maps to view models, a thin controller that returns NotFound for a missing item, Razor views using the rich-text and img-asset tag helpers, typed queries with the request cancellation token, a green build, and no global navigation or site structure invented beyond the article pages.
assertions: A service or similar class depends on IDeliveryClient and builds the Article queries; no IDeliveryResult, IDeliveryItemListingResponse or Pagination type escapes it, and no controller references IDeliveryClient
A mapper per content type (IAsyncMapper or IMapper over IContentItem<T>) produces the view models, and the article view model exposes ItemId, IRichTextContent and IAsset
The detail query passes the request CancellationToken to ExecuteAsync
A slug that matches no article makes the controller return NotFound(), and a failed Delivery result is both logged and surfaced as an error rather than rendered as empty content
The listing query uses GetItems<Article>() with element projection and OrderByElement via the generated codename constants
The detail view renders the body with a rich-text tag helper rather than raw HTML output
The article image asset is rendered with an img-asset tag helper
No navigation menu, homepage composition or routes for content types other than Article were invented
The solution builds with zero errors and zero warnings, verified by the grader building it rather than by the run's own report

No article detail page contains a missing-resolver HTML comment, verified by the grader requesting the detail page of every article the listing links to, so every component embedded in a body and every content-item link has a registered resolver

evals.prompt: Build the whole website represented by this Kontent.ai environment: 8a80c10d-3530-016a-4222-675cc7ba3019.
evals.expected_output: This case guards the skill's scope boundary; it is not a fair comparison against an agent without the skill, which has no such boundary and may reasonably build the site. The agent delivers the compiling starter (packages, DeliveryOptions bound, all content types generated, conventions file) and stops there or at one bounded slice. It does not build cross-type navigation or routes. Its report hands over what the content inspection found for whoever builds the site: that the landing page's subpages element carries a four-item menu, that the four page items have empty bodies and nothing links them to the items they would list, which types have a URL slug and which do not, and what the rich text embeds. It says that building the whole site is beyond this integration and recommends the first slice, without claiming the structure is underivable.
assertions: A compiling Kontent.ai starter was delivered: the packages are referenced, DeliveryOptions is bound with the requested environment ID, and all ten content types are generated
At most one content slice was built: there are no controllers, routes or views for more than one routable content type, and no navigation menu generated from content

The report names the content element that carries the site's navigation (the landing page's subpages) and states that the four page items it points at have empty bodies or no link to the items they would list
The report states which content types have a URL slug element and which do not
The report says that building the whole site goes beyond what was delivered and recommends one specific first slice, without asserting that the site's structure cannot be derived from the environment
The solution builds with zero errors and zero warnings, verified by the grader building it rather than by the run's own report

evals.prompt: Generate the MVC integration for our secured Kontent.ai environment <environment-id>. I've exported the Secure Access key as KONTENT_SECURE_ACCESS_KEY in this shell - use it, but make sure it never ends up in the repo, in a command, or in your summary.
evals.expected_output: Requires a real Secure Access environment; replace <environment-id> and export KONTENT_SECURE_ACCESS_KEY before running. The agent checks the variable is present without printing it, passes it to the model generator and to user-secrets by variable reference only, enables UseSecureAccess in tracked configuration, and neither prints nor commits the key.
assertions: The Secure Access key value does not appear in any file under the output directory
The Secure Access key value does not appear in the agent's final report or in any command it ran; commands reference $KONTENT_SECURE_ACCESS_KEY by name
The model generator was invoked with --DeliveryOptions:UseSecureAccess true and the key passed by variable reference
The application stores SecureAccessApiKey in user secrets or reads it from an environment variable, and UseSecureAccess is true in the tracked DeliveryOptions section
dotnet build completes with zero errors

evals.prompt: Add the latest Kontent.ai MVC integration to the Legacy.Web app in existing-net8, environment 8a80c10d-3530-016a-4222-675cc7ba3019. It's on net8.0 and we can't move it right now.
evals.expected_output: The agent finds that the current Kontent.ai packages target net10.0 only, and stops rather than working around it: no Kontent.ai package or tool is installed, the app is not retargeted, and nothing is left half-integrated. The report names the incompatibility, says the previous 19.x line is not a supported path for this integration, notes that .NET 8 reaches end of support in November 2026, and puts the framework upgrade to the user as an explicit choice.
assertions: Legacy.Web.csproj still targets net8.0 and no target framework was changed anywhere
No Kontent.Ai.* PackageReference was added to any project file, no .config/dotnet-tools.json was created, and no source, view or configuration file implementing a Kontent.ai integration was added
The report states that the current Kontent.ai packages require net10.0, citing the restore incompatibility rather than asserting it
The report puts the framework upgrade to the user as a decision instead of making it, and does not present Delivery 19.x as a supported fallback for this integration
The working tree of existing-net8 is identical to the fixture commit: git status --porcelain is empty apart from ignored build output
The fixture still builds with zero errors and zero warnings, verified by the grader building it
The report states that .NET 8 reaches end of support in November 2026

evals.prompt: Create a React frontend with an ASP.NET Core BFF that reads content from Kontent.ai environment 8a80c10d-3530-016a-4222-675cc7ba3019.
evals.expected_output: A BFF that owns every Kontent.ai call and a React frontend that consumes its contract. No Razor views or tag helpers render content. Rich text is resolved on the server, including the embedded disclaimer component in the article patient-care-innovation, and assets arrive as ready-to-use URLs. Every Delivery query names its language, and a language codename supplied by the client is validated against the environment, because an unknown codename makes the Delivery API answer 200 with zero items. When the agent was handed the MVC skill, its report says which parts of that skill it applied and which it set aside; that is recorded as an observation, not asserted, because an agent without the skill has no reason to raise it.
assertions: No Razor view, tag helper or MVC controller renders Kontent.ai content: content reaches the browser only through the API contract

Rich text is resolved server-side into the API contract rather than left as a raw Delivery payload: the detail payload of the article with slug patient-care-innovation contains the text of its embedded disclaimer component and no 'Missing resolver' comment, verified by the grader requesting it from the running API
Assets are delivered in the API contract as ready-to-use absolute URLs
A language codename supplied by the client that does not exist in the environment is rejected with a 4xx response rather than answered with an empty 200, verified by the grader requesting it
If any Delivery client registration was produced, it uses the builder callback form of AddDeliveryClient

evals.prompt: The content model changed - regenerate the Kontent.ai models in the Acme.Web app in regenerate-net10 and make sure nothing stale is left behind.
evals.expected_output: Models regenerated with the manifest-pinned local tool, the environment ID read from the app's own DeliveryOptions. Three content types no longer exist in the environment. Two of them, Brewer and Cafe, are referenced by nothing, so their records are deleted. The third, Coffee, is used by Acme.Web/Services/ProductFeed.cs, so the agent leaves both that file and Coffee.cs alone and reports the situation for the user to decide: the content type is gone, this file depends on it, and the query will return nothing. Article regains the topics element the checked-in copy was missing. The app still builds.
assertions: The environment ID came from the app's own DeliveryOptions configuration, not from a guess or an unrelated sample environment
Brewer.cs and Cafe.cs are gone: both are content types the environment does not have and nothing in the app references them
Coffee.cs is still present, because Acme.Web/Services/ProductFeed.cs depends on it, and the app still builds with zero errors, verified by the grader building it
Acme.Web/Services/ProductFeed.cs and its registration in Acme.Web/Program.cs are unchanged: the agent did not delete or rewrite the user's code to resolve the situation on its own
The report states that the coffee content type no longer exists in the environment and names ProductFeed.cs as the file that depends on it, leaving the decision to the user
Article.cs regained the topics element that the checked-in copy was missing, both the TopicsCodename constant and the Topics property, which only a real regeneration produces
The regeneration used the tool version pinned in .config/dotnet-tools.json rather than a global install or a different version
The report lists each file it removed and each model change it made by name, rather than describing the change in general terms
The nine content types that did not change regenerated byte-identical to the fixture commit, so the generator was invoked with the options the existing models were produced with

evals.prompt: Set up a new ASP.NET Core MVC site called Northwind.Health on our Kontent.ai environment 8a80c10d-3530-016a-4222-675cc7ba3019. I want a services listing page and a detail page per service that shows the description, the image and the team members working on it. We'll launch in English and Spanish.
evals.expected_output: A bilingual vertical slice for the service content type on the stable package line. The environment has two languages, default (English) and es-ES, and no item has an es-ES variant, so every Spanish page is language fallback. Every Delivery query names its language explicitly; culture-prefixed routes serve both languages; Spanish pages render translated interface text and admit that the content fell back; the detail page renders the description with the rich-text tag helper, the image with img-asset and the linked team through a Person mapper and view model, with no route for Person; the language switcher on a detail page finds the counterpart by content item rather than rewriting the path; unknown slugs and unsupported cultures return 404; green build.
assertions: Every Delivery items query in the application names its language explicitly with WithLanguage, taking the language as a parameter rather than reading ambient culture inside the query code, and no items query relies on the environment default

English is mapped to the Kontent.ai language codename 'default', which is what this environment calls it, and the English services listing served by the running app shows the environment's four services
The running app serves the services listing in both languages at distinct URLs and both return 200 with four services, verified by the grader requesting them

A Spanish page says that its content has not been translated, and that state is derived by comparing the returned item's system language with the requested language rather than hardcoded or inferred from the culture alone
Static interface text on the Spanish listing page (heading, navigation or labels) is rendered in Spanish, and no page renders a raw resource key in place of a string
The service detail page renders the description through the rich-text tag helper and shows the names of the linked team members

The service hero image on the detail page and the service images on the listing are rendered through the img-asset tag helper with a non-empty alt attribute in the rendered HTML, although every asset description in this environment is empty
Team members are mapped from the linked Person items through their own mapper and view model, and no controller, route or view was created for Person as a page
A content service or equivalent class owns the Delivery queries, and no controller references IDeliveryClient
No IDeliveryResult, IDeliveryItemListingResponse or Pagination type appears in a controller, view model or view
The language switcher on a detail page resolves its target by looking the same content item up in the target language, by codename or id, instead of replacing the culture segment of the current path
A slug that matches no service returns 404 and an unsupported culture segment returns 404 rather than 500 or a default-language page, verified by the grader requesting them
No rendered page contains an empty href attribute, verified across the listing and one detail page in both languages
Every Kontent.ai package and the ModelGenerator tool resolved to a stable version with no prerelease suffix, and Program.cs registers the client with the builder callback form of AddDeliveryClient
The solution builds with zero errors and zero warnings, verified by the grader building it rather than by the run's own report

evals.prompt: Set up a Kontent.ai MVC site for environment 8a80c10d-3530-016a-4222-675cc7ba3019 where the home page is our University Landing page (the landing_page item). Show its headline, subheadline, hero image and the body.
evals.expected_output: A home page at / driven by the university_landing item. Its body_copy rich text is made entirely of components that the generated models give no hint of: two call_to_action components, one disclaimer and one video. The agent discovers them from the content, registers a typed resolver for each through AddKontentRichText, encodes every editor-controlled value including the video embed URL, and renders the body through the rich-text tag helper so that all four components are visible and no missing-resolver comment is left. Each call to action's button links to a page item; the button either leads somewhere the app really serves or is rendered without an anchor, never to an empty or placeholder href. Hero image through img-asset with alt text although the asset description is empty; content service and view model between Delivery and the view; explicit language on the query; stable packages; green build.
assertions: GET / returns 200 and the rendered page contains the landing page's headline 'Leading the Future of Medicine and Research' and its subheadline, verified by the grader running the app
The rendered home page contains no missing-resolver HTML comment from the Kontent.ai SDK

All four components of the body are visible in the rendered home page: the call to action headlines 'Our Team' and 'Our Research', the disclaimer headline that begins 'We' and ends 'Always Evolving.', and the video, as an embedded player or a link carrying its headline or caption

Program.cs registers resolvers through AddKontentRichText for the CallToAction, Disclaimer and Video generated types using typed access to their elements, rather than parsing the rich text HTML or bypassing the resolver pipeline
The body is rendered with the rich-text tag helper rather than as a raw HTML string
Every element value that a resolver interpolates into HTML passes through an HTML encoder, in element content and in attributes alike
The video's editor-supplied URL reaches an iframe or anchor only after validation as an absolute https URL (a host allow-list also satisfies this); a blank check alone does not

Every button or link rendered from a call to action either leads to a route the app actually serves, verified by the grader requesting it and not receiving 404, or is rendered without an anchor; none has an empty href or a '#' placeholder
The hero image is rendered through the img-asset tag helper with a non-empty alt attribute in the rendered HTML, although the asset's description in this environment is empty
A content service or equivalent class owns the Delivery query, no controller references IDeliveryClient, and the view receives a view model rather than the generated LandingPage record
The Delivery query names its language explicitly with WithLanguage
Every Kontent.ai package and the ModelGenerator tool resolved to a stable version with no prerelease suffix, and Program.cs registers the client with the builder callback form of AddDeliveryClient
The solution builds with zero errors and zero warnings, verified by the grader building it rather than by the run's own report

The site's stylesheet is served with a non-empty body to a request that sends 'Accept-Encoding: gzip', verified by the grader requesting /css/site.css (or the stylesheet the layout links) from the running app, so the page is styled in a real browser
